title: Synergistic effects of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis B8762 and milk‐derived osteopontin on male reproductive health in mice
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Male reproductive health is intricately linked to dietary components and gut microbiota balance. Osteopontin (OPN) deficiency and gut dysbiosis are associated with impaired spermatogenesis, yet the synergistic effects of probiotics and OPN remain unexplored.

RESULTS

In OPN-deficient mice, combined intervention with Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis B8762 and OPN increased gut microbiota alpha diversity and upregulated key reproductive genes (Etv4, Adamts16, Prok2, Gpr55, Rad54b). Testicular histology revealed restored spermatogenic cell density and seminiferous tubule integrity.

CONCLUSION

This study demonstrates that co-administration of B8762 and OPN alleviates reproductive dysfunction via gut microbiota modulation and testicular gene regulation, offering a novel nutritional strategy for male fertility enhancement. © 2025 The Author(s).
